checks.title: Some software comes from other sources than Debian or Ubuntu
checks.detail: These sources are paused for the upgrade, since the next release may not exist on them. Docker's is put back, for the new release, after it. The others stay paused until you turn them on.

checks.title: Some containers do not start again by themselves
checks.detail: The restart of the machine stops every container, and only the ones that have a restart policy start again. These have none (no, or nothing): they stay stopped until someone starts them.

checks.title: No backup of the apps was made
checks.detail: AppManagement has no backup that succeeded: if the upgrade ends badly, the apps' data is what is lost. Make a backup of the apps first.

checks.title: The backports lines will be dropped
checks.detail: Backports are made for one release: the upgrade removes these lines, and the packages that came from them are upgraded with the rest.

checks.title: The mirrors and the security archive are checked when the plan is made
checks.detail: Whether the next release exists on each mirror, and whether the security archive still has its files, needs the network: the plan step asks, and this report does not.

checks.title: The health of the disk was not checked
checks.detail: The disk of the system did not say whether it is failing (it is a virtual disk, or its controller does not pass the question on), it sleeps and was not woken to be asked, the stack it is on has more disks than are asked, or smartctl is not installed here: this report cannot tell.

checks.title: The names of the network cards are checked before the restart
checks.detail: A new release can name the network cards differently, and a card that has another name than the one the machine's settings give it has no network. The step that comes before the restart looks at each card, and pins its name when it would change. This report does not.

checks.title: Take a snapshot, or keep a way to the console
checks.detail: An upgrade of the system cannot be undone. Before it, take a snapshot of the machine (a virtual machine's, a provider's), or be sure of a screen and a keyboard, a serial line or a console in front of it: a tunnel such as Tailscale goes down with the network card. This report cannot check that you did.

checks.title: Whether Canonical offers this upgrade is not checked here
checks.detail: Canonical opens each upgrade when it thinks it ready, and says so in metadata that is read from the network. The plan step asks for it; this report does not.
